spots.name: Porta Nigra
spots.summary: The Porta Nigra, referred to by locals as the Porta, is a large Roman city gate in Trier, Germany. It is a monumental gateway representative of Hellenistic military architecture of the time. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

spots.name: Trier Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The High Cathedral of Saint Peter in Trier, or Trier Cathedral, is a Roman Catholic cathedral in Trier, Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany. It is the oldest cathedral in Germany and the largest religious structure in Trier, notable for its long life span and grand design.

spots.name: Aula Palatina
spots.summary: The Aula Palatina, also called Basilica of Constantine, at Trier, Germany, is a Roman palace basilica and an early Christian structure built between AD 300 and 310 during the reigns of Constantius Chlorus and Constantine the Great.

spots.name: Liebfrauenkirche

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat

spots.summary: The Liebfrauenkirche in Trier, is, according to UNESCO, "the earliest church built in French High Gothic style outside France." It is designated as part of the Roman Monuments, Cathedral of St Peter and Church of Our Lady in Trier UNESCO World Heritage Site.

spots.name: Karl Marx House
spots.summary: The Karl Marx House museum is a biographical and writer's house museum in Trier. In 1818, Karl Marx, the father of Marxism, which influenced both modern socialism and communism, was born in the house. It is now a museum about Karl Marx's life and writings as well as the history of communism.

spots.name: Augusta Treverorum

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Augusta Treverorum was a Roman city on the Moselle River, from which modern Trier emerged.

spots.name: Electoral Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Electoral Palace in Trier, Germany, was the residence of the Archbishops and Electors of Trier from the 16th century until the late 18th century. It now houses various offices of the federal government and often hosts classical music concerts.

spots.name: St. Matthias' Abbey

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Matthias' Abbey is a Benedictine monastery in Trier, Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany, that belongs to the Congregation of the Annunciation.

spots.name: Saint Gangolf's Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Gangolf's Church is a Roman Catholic church in Trier, Germany. It is dedicated to St. Gangulphus, annd known for its bells. After Trier Cathedral, it is the second oldest and second tallest church building in the city.

spots.name: Roman Bridge

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Roman Bridge is an ancient structure in Trier, Germany, over the Moselle. It is the oldest standing bridge in the country, and the oldest Roman bridge north of the Alps. The nine bridge pillars date from the 2nd century AD, replacing two older, wooden bridges that date at least as far back as 17 BC.

spots.name: Karl Marx statue
spots.summary: The Karl Marx statue is a monument located on Simeonstiftplatz in Trier, Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany. It was unveiled on May 5, 2018, to mark the 200th anniversary of Karl Marx's birth in his hometown. The work by sculptor Wu Weishan is a gift from the People's Republic of China.

spots.name: Trier Imperial Baths
spots.summary: The Trier Imperial Baths are a large Roman bath complex in Trier, Germany. The complex was constructed in the early 4th century AD, during the reign of Constantine I. During that time, Trier was a major imperial hub, being a primary residence for Constantine's son Crispus.

spots.name: Rheinisches Landesmuseum Trier

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Rheinische Landesmuseum Trier is an archaeological museum in Trier, Germany. The collection stretches from prehistory through the Roman period, the Middle Ages to the Baroque era with a strong emphasis on the Roman past of Augusta Treverorum, Germany's oldest city.

spots.name: Freilichtmuseum Roscheider Hof
spots.summary: The Freilichtmuseum Roscheider Hof is an open-air museum and folklore museum in the Greater SaarLorLux Region. The museum is situated in Konz, Germany, on the Saar and Mosel rivers, 8 km west of Trier and 30 km east of Luxembourg.

spots.name: Saint Paulin Church
spots.summary: Saint Paulinus is a Baroque church in the city of Trier, Germany. Constructed between 1734 and 1753, the interior was designed by Johann Balthasar Neumann. The ceiling of the nave features a painting by the artist Christoph Thomas Scheffler.

spots.name: Trier Cathedral Treasury

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Trier Cathedral Treasury is a museum of Christian art and medieval art in Trier, Germany. The museum is owned by the Roman Catholic Diocese of Trier and is located inside the Cathedral of Trier.

spots.name: Trier Amphitheater

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Trier Amphitheater is a Roman amphitheater in Trier, Germany. It is designated as part of the Roman Monuments, Cathedral of St. Peter and Church of Our Lady in Trier UNESCO World Heritage Site as a testimony to the importance of Trier as a major Roman city north of the Alps.

spots.name: Roman Monuments, Cathedral of St Peter and Church of Our Lady in Trier
spots.summary: The Roman Monuments, Cathedral of St. Peter and Church of Our Lady in Trier are buildings and monuments of particular historical importance in Trier, Germany, that were together listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986.

spots.name: Trier Hauptbahnhof
spots.summary: Trier Hauptbahnhof is a railway station for the city of Trier, in the German state of Rhineland-Palatinate. It is a through station, about 500 metres (550 yd) east of the inner city and the Porta Nigra.

spots.name: Simeonstift of Trier

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Simeon's Collegiate Church was a collegiate church in Trier, Germany, incorporating the Porta Nigra, the Roman gate of the city. It was established some time after 1035 and dedicated to the Greek monk Simeon of Trier, who had lived in the Porta Nigra as a hermit. It was dissolved in 1802.

spots.name: Barbara Baths
spots.summary: The Barbara Baths are a large Roman bath complex in Augusta Treverorum, modern-day Trier, Germany. Stretching over 42,000 square meters, it is the largest Roman bath north of the Alps.

spots.summary: 49.752736°N 6.63766°E The Forum Baths of Trier are a ruin of a Roman bath complex in Augusta Treverorum, modern-day Trier, Germany. The baths were discovered in 1987.

spots.name: Theater Trier
spots.summary: The Theater Trier is the municipal theatre of the city of Trier and, as a three-branch house encompassing opera and musical, drama, and dance (ballet), one of the most important cultural institutions in the region. It has existed in its institutional form since 1802.
